# #line directives: the debugger and C# compiler errors point at .phrase lines
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #164, sha256:0cefb54c910115c27558ab3b2d5522ccec19a08e373fad6c9b20091a27a6cea8). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->


- **Status:** Ready
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** feature (thin slice; weighed separately from the source map by Decider D111)
- **Milestone:** Purpose: verifiability, preserved intent and reviewability
- **Source:** Split from card 161 by Decider D111 (2026-10-28): #line directives are compiler metadata and not runtime behaviour, but they put .phrase file names into debug symbols and stack traces, which is a second exposure that needs its own review.
- **Depends on:** 161
- **Story:** As Morgan, I want the C# compiler and debugger to point at .phrase lines for generated code, so that a stack trace or a build error leads straight to the spec.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given a build option phrase build --line-directives (default off), When it is on, Then the generated C# carries #line directives that map each generated method to its Phrase file base name and line, the build has zero warnings and every spec still passes
  2. Given the option off, When the demo is built, Then the generated C# contains no #line directive and no source file name, and the output is byte-identical to a build made before this card
  3. Given release builds, When the option is on, Then the card documents what the debug symbols and stack traces then expose and how to keep them out of production (exclude the PDB, or leave the option off), and a security-role reviewer signs off in the Decider record

## Context

- Only after the source map and trace command of card 161 exist; the map already covers the tracing need. Keep the option a build-time switch so the future project profile can set it per environment.
